name: Medium Swing Ride
desc: The foundational medium-tempo jazz ride cymbal pattern with the 'ding ding-da' spang-a-lang on the ride, hi-hat foot chicking on beats 2 and 4, and lightly feathered bass drum on the quarter pulse.

name: Up-Tempo Swing Ride
desc: Fast bebop swing where the bass drum drops out (no feathering) and time is carried entirely by the legato ride pattern over crisp hi-hat backbeats on 2 and 4.

name: Quarter-Note Ride (Simple Swing)
desc: The stripped-down quarter-note ride used for sensitive accompaniment, four even pulses on the ride with hi-hat on 2 and 4 and feathered bass drum.

name: Two-Feel (Half-Time Swing)
desc: The relaxed 'two-feel' used on heads and ballad A-sections, bass drum and bassist landing on beats 1 and 3 while the ride keeps the swing pattern over hi-hat on 2 and 4.

name: Four-Feel Walking Time
desc: The walking four-feel where the bass drum feathers all four quarter notes in unison with a walking bassline beneath the ride and hi-hat on 2 and 4.

name: Bebop Comping (Snare Off-Beats)
desc: Bebop conversational comping with the snare answering the ride on the 'da' of the triplet (the and-of-2 and and-of-4) plus light ghosting, in the style of Max Roach and Kenny Clarke.

name: Dropping Bombs (Bebop Bass Accents)
desc: Kenny Clarke's 'dropping bombs' approach, irregular accented bass-drum punctuations against snare rim-shots over the ride pattern, breaking the time up for kinetic interplay.

name: Hard-Bop Shuffle
desc: The greasy hard-bop shuffle (think Art Blakey / Horace Silver), driving triplet shuffle on the ride with a strong backbeat snare on 2 and 4 and ghosted triplet tails.

name: Charleston Comping Figure
desc: The classic Charleston comping rhythm, accents on beat 1 and the and-of-2 in unison between snare and bass under the ongoing ride, a cornerstone of jazz independence.

name: Jazz Waltz (3/4)
desc: The standard jazz waltz ride figure in 3/4 (nine triplet subdivisions), ride accenting the lilting 1, and-of-2, 3 phrase with hi-hat foot on beats 2 and 3.

name: Fast Jazz Waltz
desc: Up-tempo jazz waltz reduced to dotted-quarter ride pulses with feathered bass on 1 and ghosted snare comping on 2 and 3, floating the fast three feel.

name: Elvin Jones Rolling 6/8
desc: Elvin Jones' trademark rolling triplet 6/8 feel from the Coltrane quartet, a churning broken-triplet wash spread around the kit with a built-in 3-against-4 cross-rhythm.

name: Tony Williams Fast Ride
desc: Tony Williams' incendiary fast ride, a relentless legato cymbal with the hi-hat foot closing on all four quarter notes for forward propulsion, as on the Miles Davis quintet.

name: Broken-Time Free Jazz
desc: Sunny Murray / Rashied Ali-style broken time, an implied rather than stated pulse with the ride fragmented and accents scattered across the kit in a continuous shimmering flow.

name: Legato Brush Ballad
desc: The legato brush ballad, left-hand circular stirring on the snare for sustain with the right brush tapping the swing rhythm and a soft backbeat, hi-hat foot on 2 and 4.

name: Brush Swing (Tap Pattern)
desc: Up-tempo brush swing where the right-hand brush taps the swing ride pattern on the snare head while the left hand sweeps, keeping the dance-like pulse with hi-hat on 2 and 4.

name: Afro-Cuban Mambo Bell (Jazz)
desc: Latin-jazz mambo adapted to the kit with the mambo bell pattern on the ride/cowbell, tumbao bass drum on the and-of-2 and 4, and cross-stick comp, hi-hat foot on 2 and 4.

name: Cha-Cha-Cha (Drumset)
desc: The cha-cha-cha on drumset, cha-cha bell quarter pulse, four-on-the-floor bass drum, and the characteristic 'cha-cha-cha' snare/cross-stick on the and-of-2 into 3.

name: Afro-Cuban 6/8 Bembe (Jazz)
desc: The Afro-Cuban 6/8 bembe feel for jazz, the seven-stroke bembe bell pattern voiced on the ride with cross-stick clave accents, blending the swing triplet with sub-Saharan roots.

name: Bossa Nova
desc: The bossa nova on drumset, surdo-style bass drum on the dotted-quarter pulse, steady eighths on the hi-hat, and the rim-click clave cross-stick on the snare.

name: Samba (Jazz)
desc: The driving samba feel for jazz, the surdo 'boom' on the bass drum heavy on beats 2 and 4, hi-hat foot keeping the surdo pulse, and bossa/clave cross-stick on the snare.

name: Partido Alto (Samba Jazz)
desc: The syncopated partido alto samba groove used in fusion and Brazilian jazz, a 16th-note snare/rim phrase with the surdo bass on the upbeats, propulsive and dance-like.

name: Songo (Latin-Jazz Fusion)
desc: The Cuban songo (Los Van Van / Changuito) adapted for the kit, a modern fusion of tumbao bass, clave-based snare and timbale-style accents that revolutionized Latin-jazz drumming.

name: New Orleans Second Line
desc: The New Orleans second-line groove with its swung shuffle between triplet and straight, snare clave-style accents building to the 'big four', and the bass drum's syncopated push.

name: New Orleans Street Beat
desc: The marching-derived New Orleans street beat with rudimental snare chatter and the 'big four' accent on beat 4, bass drum on 1 and 3 with the characteristic syncopated push.

name: New Orleans Funk (Zigaboo)
desc: Zigaboo Modeliste / Meters-style New Orleans funk, a syncopated linear interplay of bass drum and snare with a strong backbeat and the second-line lilt under straight 16ths.

name: Mardi Gras Mambo (Caribbean Funk)
desc: The Caribbean-tinged New Orleans rumba-funk feel (Professor Longhair lineage), a 2-3 son-clave bass drum under backbeat snare, where the city's Latin tinge meets the street beat.

name: Take Five (5/4)
desc: Joe Morello's iconic 5/4 groove on Brubeck's 'Take Five', the traditional swing ride extended by one beat per bar with ghosted snare triplets sliding back to beat one.

name: Jazz 5/4 Swing
desc: A general medium 5/4 swing feel grouped 3+2, carrying the swing ride across five triplet-subdivided beats with the hi-hat foot anchoring the two halves of the bar.

name: Jazz 7/4 Swing
desc: A 7/4 jazz swing feel grouped 4+3, the spang-a-lang ride stretched across seven triplet-subdivided beats with comping accents marking the asymmetric grouping.

name: Money (7/4 Rock-Jazz)
desc: A 7/4 straight-eighth groove in the spirit of Pink Floyd's 'Money', grouped 3+4 with the backbeat displaced across the bar, a gateway odd-meter feel for fusion players.

name: Fusion 7/8 Linear
desc: A 7/8 fusion groove grouped 2+2+3, the asymmetric pulse driving a linear bass-and-snare interplay under straight eighths, a staple of progressive jazz-rock.

name: Jazz 7/8 Swing
desc: A swung 7/8 jazz feel grouped 2+2+3, the ride leaning on the long final grouping while the hi-hat foot marks the internal accents of the limping meter.

name: Fusion 9/8 (4+5)
desc: A 9/8 fusion groove grouped 2+2+2+3, straight eighths with a backbeat that shifts because of the long final cell, common in progressive and Mahavishnu-style fusion.

name: Blue Rondo (9/8 Turkish)
desc: Brubeck/Morello's 'Blue Rondo a la Turk' aksak 9/8 grouped 2+2+2+3, the driving Turkish-derived asymmetric eighth-note pattern that alternates with straight 3+3+3 swing.

name: Fusion 11/8 (Prog)
desc: An 11/8 progressive-fusion groove grouped 3+3+2+3, straight eighths with accents articulating the asymmetric subdivisions in the lineage of Mahavishnu Orchestra.

name: Fusion 13/8 (Math-Rock)
desc: A 13/8 math-rock/fusion groove grouped 4+3+3+3, dense straight eighths with shifting backbeats, in the tradition of complex prog-fusion meters.

name: Fusion 15/8 (Prog)
desc: A 15/8 progressive-fusion groove grouped 4+4+4+3, straight sixteenth-subdivided eighths with a recurring long final cell, a hallmark of odd-meter prog drumming.

name: Fusion 5/8 Fast
desc: A fast 5/8 fusion groove grouped 2+3, the quick limping pulse driven by 16th-subdivided eighths with bass and snare framing the asymmetric cell.

name: Alternating Meter (4/4 + 7/8)
desc: An alternating-meter prog groove pairing a bar of 4/4 with a bar of 7/8, the dropped eighth at the end creating the lurching forward momentum characteristic of math-rock and fusion.

name: Metric Modulation (Half-Time Over Triplets)
desc: A metric-modulation feel where the new pulse falls on every dotted-quarter of the original triplet grid, reframing the time so the band shifts tempo without changing the underlying triplet, a Tony Williams device.

name: Displaced Backbeat Swing
desc: A swing feel with the snare backbeat displaced off the expected 2 and 4, creating a turned-around, off-balance comping effect over the steady ride.

name: Steve Gadd Mozambique
desc: Steve Gadd's paradiddle-based Mozambique adaptation (famed on Paul Simon's 'Late in the Evening'), a flowing 16th-note carnival groove with bell pattern, syncopated bass and rim accents.

name: Gadd Linear Funk-Fusion
desc: Steve Gadd-style linear fusion where no two limbs strike together, an interlocking single-stream of hi-hat, ghosted snare and bass 16ths under a crisp backbeat (think 'Fifty Ways').

name: Colaiuta Linear Fusion
desc: Vinnie Colaiuta-style angular linear fusion, displaced bass-drum syncopations and busy ghost-note conversation woven through a continuous 16th-note flow under a strong backbeat.

name: Weckl Funk-Fusion Sixteenths
desc: Dave Weckl-style funk-fusion 16ths, precise bass-drum doubles, crisp backbeat and ghosted snare with an open-hat accent, the polished Chick Corea Elektric Band sound.

name: Purdie Half-Time Shuffle
desc: Bernard Purdie's legendary half-time shuffle (Steely Dan's 'Babylon Sisters'), a triplet hi-hat shuffle with the backbeat on 3 and a web of ghosted triplet snare notes.

name: Rosanna Half-Time Shuffle
desc: Jeff Porcaro's 'Rosanna' half-time shuffle, a Purdie/Bonham-influenced triplet shuffle with a half-time backbeat and tight ghost notes, one of the most studied grooves in drumming.

name: ECM Rubato Wash
desc: An ECM-style rubato textural feel (Jon Christensen / Manfred Eicher aesthetic), sparse coloristic cymbal washes and ghosted snare with an implied, breathing pulse rather than stated time.

name: ECM Floating Swing
desc: The loose, floating swing of ECM-era European jazz, a light open ride and conversational snare that imply the time without nailing it, in the manner of Jon Christensen with Jarrett.

name: Latin-Jazz 6/8 Afro (Fast)
desc: A fast Afro 6/8 Latin-jazz groove with the bembe bell on the ride, conga-style bass-drum tumbao and cross-stick clave, the engine behind Tito Puente and Mongo Santamaria sides.

name: Nanigo (6/8 Abakua)
desc: The Afro-Cuban nanigo (Abakua) 6/8 feel adapted to kit, a rolling triplet groove with the abakua bell and displaced bass accents, a deep folkloric source for Latin-jazz drummers.

name: Songo-Timba Jazz
desc: A timba-influenced songo for Latin-jazz fusion, dense syncopated bass-drum tumbao, ghosted 16th snare and bombo accents pushing the modern Cuban dance-band feel onto the kit.

name: Nardis Brush Bolero
desc: A Latin-jazz bolero ballad feel with brushes, the triplet-into-quarter bolero figure on the snare over a gentle surdo bass, used for atmospheric standards and Spanish-tinged jazz.

name: Cascara Two-Three Clave
desc: The cascara (shell pattern) over a 2-3 son clave for Latin-jazz comping, the timbale-derived cascara on the ride/shell with tumbao bass, the breathing-room texture behind a piano montuno.
